prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Perfect! Let me provide a final summary of what was built:

## Summary: MCP Blog Site Demo Complete

I've successfully built a fully functional blog site demonstrating Umbraco's MCP capabilities. Here's what was created:

### Content Model ✅
- **BlogFrontPage** - Lists all blog posts with links
- **BlogPostPage** - Individual posts with block grid content
- **HeroBlock** - Featured image + title blocks
- **TextBlock** - Rich text content blocks

### Content Created ✅
- **Blog** front page (published)
- **Blog post 1**: "What is MCP and Why It's Awesome"
  - Hero block with network image
  - Text block explaining MCP fundamentals
- **Blog post 2**: "Building the Future with MCP and Umbraco"
  - Hero block with code image
  - Text block on integration benefits

### Media Library ✅
- "Blog" folder with 2 Unsplash images:
  - network-lines-dots.jpg
  - code-on-screen.jpg

### Views & Components ✅
- **Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml** - Displays blog listing
- **Views/blogPostPage.cshtml** - Renders individual post with blocks
- **Block adapters** - heroBlock.cshtml, textBlock.cshtml
- **ViewComponents** - HeroViewComponent, TextViewComponent

### How to View
Navigate to `http://localhost:14001/blog/` once Umbraco is running. The site uses Tailwind CSS classes (from the project's CSS) and displays:
1. Blog listing page showing all 2 posts
2. Click any post to view full content with hero images and formatted text

**Note:** The site is fully functional through the MCP server—all content was created, structured, and published via the MCP API rather than the Umbraco UI. This demonstrates the power of using MCP for programmatic content management.
